normalization_provenance: the tile is np.clip(tile, 0, max_clip_value) and then A.ToFloat(max_value=max_clip_value)
the divisor is the clip value, not 255
input_contract.scale_note: training_pixel_um is set to the scale of the reference PHerc0139 prediction this recipe produced, so the source runs native and the runner performs no resample; the published recipe does not state a single canonical training micron
input_contract.normalization: divide by 255, no clip -- what this recipe's own runner does
input_contract.depth_sampling: consecutive source layers centred on the stack; no resampling

comparability: this lane is scale-restricted: it was exercised at approximately 2 um and must not be routed to the 8.64/9.362 um target cohort without its own control at that scale
single depth centre per invocation: this lane has no built-in stability aggregation
not bit-comparable with @1.0.0 receipts: different preprocessing, same checkpoint

why_this_version: the recipe ships its own runner and 1.0.0 named the generic one
the generic runner normalises clip(0,200)/200 and this recipe divides by 255 with no clip
the generic runner resamples the depth axis, and at a ratio of 1.0 that samples half-integer positions -- every plane the average of two layers -- where this recipe takes consecutive layers
the generic runner blends tiles uniformly and this recipe blends them under a Hann window
measured 2026-07-28: under 1.0.0 the map correlates r=0.079 with the community map published for this very recipe, on ground where our render matches theirs at r=0.98
